note.text: Earth's main compositional layers are crust, mantle and core. The crust is the thin outer layer; the mantle beneath it is mostly solid rock that can flow very slowly over geological time. The core is largely iron-rich material: its outer part is liquid and its inner part solid. The lithosphere is a mechanical layer including crust and uppermost mantle, not a synonym for crust alone. Much evidence comes from seismic waves and other indirect observations, not a borehole reaching the core.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A schematic cross-section helps a class in Buea distinguish layers, but the diagram is not to scale. The thin crust would otherwise be difficult to show. Do not interpret the whole mantle as an open underground sea of liquid lava. Different temperatures, pressures and material properties explain why layers behave differently.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: State whether a classification concerns composition or mechanical behaviour. Identify crust, mantle, outer core and inner core without swapping solid and liquid. A drawing illustrates a model; examine the observations supporting that model rather than treating coloured bands as direct photographs of the interior.
